issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]) but the solution's Bookstore class declares init(books: [Book], valid: Bool). The solution's Client calls Bookstore(books: books) (single parameter), so the constructor signature in the solution is inconsistent with the specification and with the usage in Client. This mismatch would prevent successful compilation and confuses students about the required constructor API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer signature match the problem specification: change the Bookstore init to init(books: [Book]) (remove the extraneous 'valid: Bool' parameter). Ensure the template and solution both provide the same constructor signature so Client can construct Bookstore(books:). Alternatively, if an extra parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and all call sites to reflect the required parameters.

issues.description: The problem specification requires a Bookstore initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md), but the solution's Bookstore class defines an initializer with an extra parameter init(books: [Book], valid: Bool). This introduces an unexpected identifier/parameter ('valid') and an API mismatch — the solution's Client even calls Bookstore(books: books) without the extra parameter. Students following the problem will expect to construct a Bookstore with a single books parameter; the extra 'valid' parameter in the solution creates confusion and breaks the direct mapping between the required API and the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Bookstore initializer with the problem specification by removing the extra parameter. Change the initializer in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift to init(books: [Book]) so students can construct a Bookstore with Bookstore(books: books). Alternatively, if an additional parameter is required, update the problem statement and all call sites (e.g. Client) to use the same initializer name and parameters, or provide a default value for the extra parameter to preserve the single-parameter constructor.
